To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the temperature of the trunk, arm, and leg decreased by about 1°C, whereas the temperature in the hand and the foot increased by about 3°C following total spinal anesthesia; and 2) the mean blood flow in the upper arm (C7 area) decreased to 26, 61, and 52% of the control value, 15 min following total spinal anesthesia.
the skin temperature and blood ﬂow decreased in the truncal region, while the skin temperature and ﬂow increased in the extremities following total spinal anaesthetic block.
extensive sympathetic blockade during total spinal anesthesia induces regional different changes of the skin temperature and decrease of the skin blood flow of the truncal region.

the study of the influence of the sympathetic nervous system on the microcirculation.

the effects of spinal anesthesia on the cardiovascular system are complex, and the effects of spinal block on the cardiovascular system depend upon the level of the block, the dose of local anesthetic, the patient's position, the presence or absence of preexisting cardiovascular disease, the presence of other medications that affect the cardiovascular system, and the presence or absence or the degree of sympathetic blockade.

the sympathetic nervous system plays a major role in maintaining the normal temperature of the skin.

the skin of the trunk is more sensitive than the skin of the limbs and the face.
